status: candidate: generated and validated by rule from licensed lexical data, without a person's approval of each word. Only high-confidence words are used as independent evidence, and a result on them is provisional, never verified mastery. Difficulty is a feature-based estimate, not calibrated.

sources.name: English Speller Database (ESDB, formerly SCOWL), by Kevin Atkinson
sources.licence: MIT-like permissive licence; notices kept verbatim (including the UKACD and WordNet notices)
sources.used_for: words, commonness (size 10/20/35), British spelling and accepted variants, part of speech, inflected forms

sources.name: The CMU Pronouncing Dictionary, Carnegie Mellon University
sources.used_for: syllables and stress (doubling rules), homophone groups

sources.name: Open English WordNet (derived from Princeton WordNet), by the Open English Wordnet team
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0, plus the Princeton WordNet licence for the underlying data
sources.used_for: short meanings (clues), example sentences (homophones), relations confirming prefix and suffix joins

filters.scowl_usage_notes: groups marked vulgar, offensive, informal or nonstandard are excluded

policy.evidence: high-confidence assess, retention and contrast words only

confidence.high: SCOWL list 35, UK frequency tag on the word or its base, unambiguous pronunciation, a rule-made misspelling exists
confidence.medium: less common (list 50), no frequency tag, an accepted American variant, or no specific misspelling
confidence.low: CMUdict pronunciations disagree on syllables or stress (e.g. record, present)
